decisive_items: RT-PCR tests from nasopharyngeal swabs: positive (Feb 8)
close contact with grandmother who had rhinorrhea and throat irritation
response.rationale: Positive RT-PCR in a 3-month-old with upper respiratory symptoms and low-grade fever most strongly supports RSV, a common viral pathogen in infants. Other candidates lack confirmatory testing or are contradicted by negative influenza panel.

rejected.why: No confirmatory evidence; normal oxygen saturation and lack of lower tract signs make pneumonia less specific.
Describes syndrome but not etiologic agent; RT-PCR positivity favors a specific viral diagnosis.
Fever is nonspecific and not a diagnosis.
Common cold is a clinical label without confirmatory test; RT-PCR positivity suggests a specific virus.
Adenovirus not confirmed; negative respiratory panel and no specific test.
Pharyngitis not supported by exam findings; symptoms are rhinorrhea and congestion.
